chapter: Idaho tours, Music Town and retirement
title: Biddy Mason, her life and good works in Los Angeles
summary: The former slave Biddy Mason won her freedom in court, fed the poor, founded the church that became First A.M.E., and inspired Spikes's screenplay.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, and when the big flood was, that's where she must have bought the groceries there because the history of her says that on Spring Street the grocery, and he was at Fifth, and she lived between Third and Fourth, so she musta walked down to that grocery.
Biddy Mason being one of the founding citizens of Los Angeles and a former slave who walked here from Georgia, you told me, right?

Yes. Driving a head...three or four hundred head of sheep. That was her job. And she was freed after being hidden out in the mountains here for several years--three or four years --and they found her and found the group out there and carried them into court, and she was freed. And from that time on, she became
one of the...I don't know what you'd call it...she was one of the... I guess you'd call it "humaninists"...what do you call it? Humanists?

Humanists. Because she fed the poor, took care of the children, and she organized the church in her own little home and then got money and built another church on Fourth and Grand, I think it was. Then she moved on First and Main Street in a building, then they built a...they got enough together and they built another big church bigger, and it's...the church is still operating.
The First A.M.E.--the First African Methodist Episcopal Church of Los Angeles.
And it's now a very, very large church.

Yeah, and it's...I think the building over there is worth three or four million now, and the property and everything, but it all started in that little...but she done so much good and like that. She visited the sick, and she took care of the prisoners that was in the jails, carried them sandwiches and sang in a little group of singers and praying for them on the streets at the gambling houses and everything. She went in with her little...like a Salvation Army used to do, and I guess she started all that. I don't know.
And you've written a screenplay about her. When did you start writing? When you retired from real estate?
Oh, I wrote before that. I told you I had "Jump, Jive and Jam," "Harlemlesque" and those things before that but
after I retired, why I got permission to write Biddy Mason, you know.
